title: Cursor pricing: billing basis and cost boundaries
summary: Cursor pricing: billing basis and cost boundaries. Separate the recorded base price from unverified usage and operating costs.

sections.heading: One developer on a monthly plan
paragraphs: The recorded base is not a promise of unlimited model use. Before estimating a month of work, record the models, agent intensity and on-demand billing setting. Tax and overage remain outside a simple base-price comparison.

sections.heading: A team purchase
paragraphs: Multiply only a verified per-seat price by the actual seat count. Do not substitute an individual plan when administration or team privacy controls are required.

sections.heading: No task-to-credit exchange rate
paragraphs: A request, a credit and a token are not interchangeable. ToolPilot has not measured a representative workload across these products, so this guide does not invent a shared usage conversion or promise a fixed number of completed tasks.

verdict: Start with the individual subscription, then account for usage beyond the included allowance.
bestFor: Buyers checking Cursor subscription and usage assumptions
notFor: Readers seeking a guaranteed workload total without measuring usage
migration: Trial the candidate on a branch; retain the original workflow until tests, export and billing checks pass.
gaps: Verify the account's Privacy Mode and team setting, use of personal API keys, enabled non-ZDR model approvals, Cloud Agent use and applicable agreement before drawing account-specific processing or retention conclusions; no account settings were inspected.

pros.text: Cursor says every plan includes a set amount of model usage and documents on-demand usage after that amount is consumed.
The pricing page distinguishes self-serve card payments from invoice-based Enterprise billing, which helps define the quote to request.

cons.text: On-demand model usage is billed in arrears, so the plan base amount alone does not represent total spend for a high-usage month.
The included model allowance and applicable taxes depend on current plan and billing details; verify the chosen plan before budgeting.

faqs.question: What happens after the included model usage is consumed?
faqs.answer: Cursor documents optional on-demand usage billed in arrears. Check its current terms and spending controls before relying on continued usage.

faqs.question: Does the listed plan price guarantee a fixed monthly total?
faqs.answer: No. The pricing page describes included model usage and additional on-demand billing; estimate workload separately and verify tax and plan terms.

faqs.question: What does Cursor Privacy Mode cover, and what should an account verify?
faqs.answer: Cursor says Privacy Mode prevents training on Customer Data and that most model requests use provider zero-data-retention agreements, subject to safety and abuse review and non-ZDR model exceptions. Requests made with personal API keys still pass through Cursor's backend and rely on the provider's terms for retention. Optional Cloud Agents store encrypted repository copies while a run is active, then delete them after completion. Teams and Enterprise can enforce Privacy Mode; Cursor says individual plans follow its Privacy Policy rather than the commercial DPA. Verify the account setting, organization policy, model approvals, API-key route, Cloud Agent use and applicable agreement; none was inspected here. Cursor also says Privacy Mode applies to Self-Hosted Machines and that code sent by the worker is not used for training when enabled, although run content still reaches Cursor and artifacts may upload to its storage; confirm whether this feature and setting apply to the account.

faqs.question: Does a self-hosted Cursor worker remove infrastructure costs?
faqs.answer: No. Cursor says managed Cloud Agents include execution infrastructure, while Self-Hosted Machines require you to pay for and operate the machines, containers or cluster; selected-model usage follows its pricing. No account quote or workload was tested.
